heading: Are superposed features one-dimensional directions rather than multi-dimensional structures?
definition: what is superposed are 1-D directions (vs. multi-dimensional features).
summary: Several independent groups find features that do not reduce to single directions, such as cyclic day and month representations in Mistral 7B and Llama 3 8B and ring-shaped structure in Gemma 2. Single directions still work for some features, such as sentiment, so the claim that superposed features are always one-dimensional is contested.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy/synthetic: conditional directional support, without a scale-wide replication level established by these records. <1B: ? for exclusivity, with prior-dependent scope limits in explicitly sized Qwen3.5-0.8B. 1-10B: C. 10-100B and >100B: ?, without explicitly sized coverage. GPT-2-small findings are retained without assigning an unstated parameter count.
suggested_status.reason: The exclusive directional claim faces statistical and causal counterevidence from calendar representations in Mistral 7B and Llama 3 8B (arXiv:2405.14860#R4–R11). Directional ground-truth month features remain recoverable in the constructed BOWS setting (arXiv:2603.09972#R6–R7), and sentiment dimension comparisons support useful single directions (10.18653/v1/2024.blackboxnlp-1.5#r4–r6), without establishing universality. Explicit <1B evidence is prior-dependent (arXiv:2605.08891#R1–R2). counts.json was built before the checks and has not been rebuilt: versions.V6.studies_tested = 26, versions.V6.studies_with_challenges = 6 and versions.V6.studies_with_limits_scope = 18 still count the pre-check labels and relations. After the checks, the against section has challenges verdicts from arXiv:2405.14860, arXiv:2605.09224, arXiv:2505.18235, arXiv:2606.25234, arXiv:2610.20767, arXiv:2610.20840 and arXiv:2504.20197. The checks moved arXiv:2505.18235 and arXiv:2504.20197 there from limits_scope, and moved arXiv:2604.28119 from challenges to limits_scope. Limits_scope verdicts come from arXiv:2604.28119, arXiv:2605.09224 (Gemma 2 9B layer-11 random sample, formerly supports), arXiv:2610.20840 (real-data gripper steering), 10.18653/v1/2024.blackboxnlp-1.5, arXiv:2605.08891 and lw:roE7SHjFWEoMcGZKd. arXiv:2606.25234 and arXiv:2610.20767 keep their challenges verdicts, but the checks set their limits_scope verdicts to none. The checks set every V6 verdict of arXiv:2602.02315, arXiv:2607.04167, arXiv:2606.12138, arXiv:2503.01822, arXiv:2606.06333, arXiv:2605.18537, lw:JfJ4WTRHmooPBWRFv, arXiv:2510.08638, arXiv:2410.14670 and lw:ctGeJGHg9pbc8memF to none, and changed the relation of arXiv:2602.02315 to discusses and of arXiv:2605.18537 to uses_without_test; the pre-check counts still include them. The 1-10B C rests on challenges in arXiv:2405.14860 (Mistral 7B, Llama 3 8B), arXiv:2605.09224 (Gemma 2 2B and 9B) and arXiv:2505.18235 (Mistral 7B layer 8). arXiv:2504.20197's challenge is a theoretical prediction, not a trained-network measurement. versions.V6.studies_by_size, also built before the checks, lacks explicit 10-100B and >100B entries.
suggested_status.open_questions: A result distinguishing irreducible multidimensional units from correlated or grouped directional features, demonstrating their superposition in a learned model, and comparing causal adequacy at matched capacity would sharpen this status. Representative prevalence measurements and explicitly larger-model tests would establish its scope.

source.title: Toy Models of Superposition
source.authors: Nelson Elhage; Tristan Hume; Catherine Olsson; Nicholas Schiefer; T. Henighan; S. Kravec; Zac Hatfield-Dodds; R. Lasenby; Dawn Drain; Carol Chen; R. Grosse; Sam McCandlish; J. Kaplan; D. Amodei; M. Wattenberg; Chris Olah

original_result.result: The original paper did not test this claim.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Families of related sparse autoencoder (SAE) features were linear combinations of 1-D directions, not curved manifolds.
Extra subspace dimensions added nothing over a single sentiment direction in Pythia and GPT-2.
Each connection between maze cells was decoded by one SAE feature, read as one residual direction.
In a ReLU autoencoder, superposed 1-D directions jointly produced a circular arrangement of months.
Mean activations for each bracket depth and table column lay along one dominant principal component.
In Gemma 2 9B layer 11, six of ten random autoencoder experts were near-linear, orthogonal directions.
In decision transformer MemoryDT, one PCA direction split key from ball instructions and reproduced adversarial effects.
Steering activations along single directions shifted vision-language model captions predictably toward target ImageNet classes.
One dominant component decoded MolmoBot's robot gripper command nearly as well as the full activation vector.
Linearly unpredictable sparse autoencoder error in Gemma and Llama looked unlike sparse sums of linear features.
One sentiment direction captured most, but not all, sentiment information in Pythia-2.8b and GPT2-small.
A purely theoretical random-lattice model predicts about 4-D component features but possibly 1-D context features.
Colours, dates, years, months and weekdays formed loops or curves spanning several dimensions.
Mean activations for indentation, Gemma table rows and numeric magnitude needed two to five principal components.
Single SAE latents nearly matched multi-dimensional feature blocks in geometric steering, and transferred visual steering better.
Continuous concepts (release year, US geographic coordinates) in Llama 2-7b each spanned several linearly predictable directions.
One rank-6 subspace learned by a subspace-aware SAE covered GPT-2 Small's temporal concepts, with seasons ordered.
Llama-3.2-1B represented the mean of numbers in its prompt on a curved, multi-directional manifold.
A hand-built network superposed multi-dimensional subspaces, so in principle superposition does not require 1-D directions.
GPT-2 small position forms a roughly 3-D helix that SAEs split into many features.
In a toy transformer, co-active units were multi-dimensional belief-state subspaces that switched on and off sparsely.
Parts of speech in a PCFG-trained transformer showed differing effective dimensions.
Preliminary DINOv2 evidence hinted that features occupy convex regions rather than lying purely along directions.
Most bilinear-autoencoder features on Qwen3.5-0.8B spanned very few dimensions, but a tail spanned more.
DINOv3 feature-dimension estimates depended on the feature-extraction method; some came close to a single direction.
GPT-2 SAE features that changed with the SAE seed still recurred as subspaces, not individual directions.
Top component of real-data gripper steering vectors held 31–59% of variance; editing it disturbed arm joints.
Days, months and years formed irreducible 2-D circular features in GPT-2 small and Mistral 7B.
Continuous concepts in Llama3.1-8B lay on curved manifolds that sparse autoencoder (SAE) atoms only tiled locally.
In robot vision-language-action models, feature blocks had about 5.3 effective dimensions; SAEs split selected nonlinear manifolds.
Gemma 2 autoencoder experts showed rings and periodicity; in two random samples, most experts were nonlinear.
DINOv3 feature blocks had about 2–4 effective dimensions; multi-dimensional codes compressed better than 1-D SAEs.
In robot models, target distance used two near-orthogonal, range-specific directions; wrist roll traced a curved arc.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Whether the recovered multidimensional units in learned models are themselves stored in superposition with other features, with an explicit feature-capacity comparison.
untested.basis: The pack's untested-parts lines for arXiv:2605.09224 and arXiv:2602.02315 leave this open. For arXiv:2602.02315 the checker notes the paper itself does not frame this as an open question; its corrections record that superposition of its belief manifolds with other features is not measured. Context from arXiv:2602.02315, whose rows are cannot_determine for V6 after the checks (both V6 verdicts none; relation discusses; tranche T6): Llama-3.2-1B on in-context Gaussian time series at com2num tokens shows smooth, substantially curved belief manifolds (arXiv:2602.02315#r1); probe transfer is local and decays with distance in mean (arXiv:2602.02315#r12); readout-field dimensionality, which concerns probe directions, increases with depth and drops at the final layer (arXiv:2602.02315#r13); spline-based additive interpolation from the anchored mean and standard-deviation manifolds fails to reproduce the joint sheet, leaving other decompositions possible (arXiv:2602.02315#r14). Further base models (LFM2-1.2B, Llama-3.1-8B, OLMo-2-0425-1B, OLMo-2-1124-7B, OLMo-3-1025-7B; PCA after the second layer and at penultimate and final layers) give qualitative structured-manifold results without quantitative dimensionality estimates (arXiv:2602.02315#r2, arXiv:2602.02315#r5, arXiv:2602.02315#r7, arXiv:2602.02315#r8, arXiv:2602.02315#r9). arXiv:2610.20767 and arXiv:2610.20840 measure recovered feature geometry, behavioural relevance and activation interventions. Neither tests superposition of the recovered units or compares represented feature count with representational capacity, and neither raises this as an open question, so for these two it is a scope inference, not an author statement. The theoretical construction does not answer the learned-model question. counts: versions.V6.main_rows_by_operation contains measurement, probing, patching, addition, removal and other, without a training or scaling category.

untested.what: Representative prevalence of directional versus irreducibly multidimensional features across a model's full feature population.
untested.basis: Calendar and templated-concept studies identify selected examples; SMIXAE's random expert review is preliminary and estimator-specific. None establishes model-wide prevalence of irreducible feature types. counts: versions.V6.studies_with_untested_parts = 26; the relevant untested-parts lines concern prevalence or generalization beyond selected concepts.

untested.what: Dimensionality tests in explicitly identified 10–100B and >100B models.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V6.studies_by_size has entries for <1B, 1-10B and not stated, without 10-100B or >100B entries. Unspecified sizes prevent inferring complete absence at those scales.

untested.what: Matched longitudinal tests of feature dimensionality through pretraining, instruction tuning and preference training.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V6.studies_by_stage includes base, instruct/chat and preference/RL settings, so those stages are represented. However, versions.V6.main_rows_by_operation contains no training category, and the pack does not supply a matched stage-transition experiment.

untested.what: Whether the multidimensional concept groups and belief subspaces measured in these studies are irreducible feature units or collections of 1-D directional features. The measured objects are PCFG part-of-speech subspaces, a six-vector GPT-2 Small SASA temporal group, rotated Llama 2-7b time and space components, and belief cones in a toy transformer. None of these studies applies a test that separates one irreducible multidimensional unit from several directional features, and none establishes that the measured groups are stored in superposition.
untested.basis: After the checks, each of these studies' V6 verdicts is none and the cited rows are cannot_determine for V6. arXiv:2503.01822#R15: in a two-layer, width-128 transformer trained on an English PCFG (middle residual stream), parts of speech require differing numbers of dimensions to capture 99% of variance; the checker notes that this does not distinguish irreducible multidimensional features from collections of 1-D features, and that feature irreducibility is untested. arXiv:2606.06333#r17: in GPT-2 Small layer 7, SASA group 1473 contains six decoder vectors and responds to multiple temporal categories (days, months, years, seasons); the checker notes that the group can contain several 1-D features. arXiv:2605.18537#R2 and arXiv:2605.18537#R3: Llama 2-7b layer 16 Varimax rotation of the top 5 time features and top 32 space features gives decade separation and state localization; Section 4.1 reports multiple linearly predictable scalar features of each concept; the checker changes its relation to uses_without_test. lw:JfJ4WTRHmooPBWRFv#r3 and lw:JfJ4WTRHmooPBWRFv#r4: in a four-layer decoder-only transformer trained on an equal-weight mixture of two Mess3 HMMs, two posterior-scaled cones are 3-D projections of a 5-D belief geometry, and effective dimensionality is component-dependent, with no numerical cumulative-variance values. Neither row establishes superposition or excludes a decomposition into 1-D directions, though the authors propose restating sparse 1-D features as sparse multidimensional subspaces. The layer is final-layer per the main text and third of four blocks per the appendix. Its entropy-filtering facts are in method_sensitivity. This item covers these groups only; calendar clusters given a statistical irreducibility test are in V6 against. counts: versions.V6.verdicts.limits_scope (studies 18) was built before the checks and still counts these studies' original limits_scope verdicts.

untested.what: Dimensionality of the individual features behind ordinal-task centroid geometry in Gemma-2-2B, Gemma-2-9B and Qwen3-4B. PCA of per-value mean activations gives directional centroids for some task variables and higher-dimensional centroids for others. Neither outcome determines whether the underlying superposed features are 1-D or irreducibly multidimensional.
untested.basis: After the checks, arXiv:2607.04167's V6 verdicts (supports and limits_scope) are both none, and rows r9–r14 are cannot_determine for V6. The paper's Sections 3.2 and 5 separate centroid geometry from token-level representations, and the checker notes that higher-dimensional class means can arise from multiple 1-D features. Directional centroids: bracket-depth and table-column centroids have more than 90% of their variance on PC1 in all three models at middle-to-late layers (arXiv:2607.04167#r9, arXiv:2607.04167#r10), and Qwen3-4B table-row centroids collapse to 1-D at middle layers (arXiv:2607.04167#r12). Higher-dimensional centroids (Section 4.1, PCs for 90% of centroid variance): indentation 2–3 PCs with PC1 approximately 47–54% (arXiv:2607.04167#r11); Gemma table rows 3–4 PCs (arXiv:2607.04167#r13); numeric magnitude 4–5 PCs with PC1 40–62% and no clear ordinal progression (arXiv:2607.04167#r14). The Figure 4 caption conflicts with Section 4.1 by listing Qwen3-4B indentation among the cases that collapse to 1-D at middle layers. counts: versions.V6.verdicts.supports (studies 9) and versions.V6.verdicts.limits_scope (studies 18) were built before the checks and still include this study's original verdicts.

wording_issues.issue: V6 is about superposed units. These studies measure the geometry of recovered multidimensional units, and some also intervene on them: SMIXAE experts in Gemma 2; Gaussian-belief manifolds and steering in Llama-3.2-1B; block features and supervised representation geometry in robot policies. None tests whether those units are superposed with other features. For the belief-manifold study and both robot studies, this gap is a scope inference rather than something the authors say. The belief-manifold study's Appendix E.4 finds that one additive decomposition (spline interpolation from the anchored mean and standard-deviation manifolds) fails to reproduce the joint sheet, and it allows other decompositions. The same study's PCA of further base models (LFM2-1.2B, LFM2-2.6B, LFM2.5-1.2B-Base, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-3B, OLMo-2-0425-1B, OLMo-2-1124-7B, OLMo-3-1025-7B) reports qualitatively structured belief manifolds. It does not measure their dimensionality or whether they are superposed. The block-feature study's stated limitations are about something else: feature emergence, participation in policy computation and intervention generalization.

Intrinsic manifold dimension differs from linear-subspace dimension. GPT2-small layer-7 years are intrinsically 1-D, but along a curve, not a fixed direction. gpt2-small layer-0 positional embeddings (positions 1–127) form a helical manifold that the authors call one-dimensional, yet its top three PCs explain 95% of variance. Llama-3.2-1B Gaussian-belief manifolds are curved, and probes for the mean transfer only locally, decaying with distance in mean. Readout dimension is a third, separate measure: in the same study the readout fields are multidirectional, and their dimensionality rises with depth and drops at the final layer. This dimensionality is about probe directions, not stored units. The positional and belief-manifold rows do not show that these manifolds are superposed units (V6 state: cannot_determine). They illustrate the distinction without testing V6.

The records use 'feature' for binary ground-truth variables, semantic concepts, SAE atoms and learned blocks. Several directions for one concept do not show that the concept is one irreducible unit. In the middle residual stream of a two-layer Transformer trained on an English PCFG, different parts of speech need different numbers of dimensions to capture 99% of variance. In GPT-2 Small layer 7, SASA group 1473 has six decoder vectors that respond to several temporal categories. In Llama 2-7b layer 16, Varimax rotation of the top 5 time features and the top 32 space features gives several interpretable components. That paper itself treats one concept as having several linearly predictable scalar features (Section 4.1). None of these results separates one multidimensional feature from several directional ones, and the checks set these studies' V6 verdicts to none. The reverse case also occurs: in the BOWS autoencoder, binary month variables each sit along their own direction (per-feature R² = 0.98) and together form a circle.

The either/or contrast does not fit a single model and layer that holds both kinds. In Gemma 2 9B layer 11, manual review of a random SMIXAE expert sample classified 6/10 experts as approximately linear, 2/10 as nonlinear and 2/10 as noise. Random samples in Gemma 2 2B layer 12 and Gemma 2 9B layer 20 each contain 6/10 nonlinear experts. These samples are small and classified by hand. The nonlinear encoder and the lack of control baselines also limit how far the geometry can be attributed to the model's own feature units.

A useful control or readout direction can capture only part of a representation. Sentiment information remains after directional ablation, and gripper control can succeed along one component despite distributed steering variance and arm-joint leakage.

method_sensitivity.factor: Data setting and model (simulated vs real-robot gripper steering)
method_sensitivity.what: Gripper steering-vector variance is more concentrated in one component in simulation than on real data. In simulated MolmoBot (action expert layer 32, natural-rollout landmarks), PC1 captures approximately 70% of steering-vector variance. On real-world DROID episodes (final action-expert block), PC1 explains 59% in π0.5 (stable rank 1.69) and 31% in MolmoAct2 (stable rank 3.21). Model and data source change together, so the comparison isolates neither factor. Steering-vector variance is an indirect measure of feature dimensionality.

SMIXAE random-sample geometry changes across Gemma model-layer settings. Its Gemma 2 9B layer-20 top newline periodic-minus-linear ΔR² is 0.507 at line length 80 characters and 0.320 at 150 characters. LlaVA-Next directional caption steering is stronger at earlier layers.

method_sensitivity.factor: Featurizer prior, block dimension and sparsity
method_sensitivity.what: Bilinear composite and quadratic priors produce different rank structures. Vision block-code rank and description-length optima depend on the featurizer and allotted dimension. Robot BSF results likewise depend on block dimension and featurizer; those ranks alone do not establish ground-truth feature units.

Additional DAS dimensions can improve fitting-distribution patching without improving transfer. Pythia-1.4b Treebank logit-difference changes decrease across the reported 1-D, 2-D and 3-D settings; the pack identifies overfitting as a possible contributor.

The GPT2-small year visualization uses unit-normalized representations; Mistral calendar trajectories retain structure in the third principal component. The verdict also reports that year-isometry conclusions depend on ordinary versus logarithmic distance. Intrinsic dimensionality, planar appearance and fixed-direction dimensionality consequently require distinct measurements.

In a four-layer decoder-only transformer trained on an equal-weight nonergodic mixture of two Mess3 HMM components, stricter posterior-entropy filtering of converged-model activations produces faster PCA cumulative-variance accumulation and suppresses the less-supported component cone. No numerical cumulative-variance values are reported. The two co-active component cones seen in early training are 3-D projections of a 5-D belief geometry. The pack also records, without a row, cleaner canonical geometry under small initialization. For V6 these rows are cannot_determine and the study has no V6 verdict: the measured belief-geometry dimensionality neither establishes superposition nor separates multidimensional superposed features from a decomposition into 1-D directions. The analysed layer is stated inconsistently: final layer in the main text, third of four blocks in the appendix.

Correlated month-word variables in the bag-of-words autoencoder yield circular geometry while remaining linearly decodable directional features. The circle itself is insufficient to distinguish this mechanism from an irreducible multidimensional concept.

method_sensitivity.factor: SAE clustering threshold and intervention layer
method_sensitivity.what: The circular-feature study reports that the Mistral weekday cluster's appearance depends on the similarity threshold. Circular-subspace intervention effects in Mistral 7B and Llama 3 8B (training stage not stated), on the weekday and month tasks at the α token, also vary across layers. Early-layer effects nearly match whole-layer patching.

method_sensitivity.factor: Task variable and model (ordinal centroid PCA; context only, no V6 verdict)
method_sensitivity.what: Context only. arXiv:2607.04167 has no V6 verdict, and its rows are cannot_determine for V6: PCA of class means does not measure individual feature dimensionality, and higher-dimensional means can arise from multiple 1-D features. In Gemma-2-2B (2.6B), Gemma-2-9B (9.2B) and Qwen3-4B (4.0B), training stage not stated, centroid geometry varies by task variable and model. For bracket depth and table columns at mid-to-late layers, PC1 captures more than 90% of centroid variance in all three models. Qwen3-4B table rows collapse to 1-D at mid-layers. Section 4.1 reports these PC counts for 90% of variance: indentation 2–3 (PC1 approximately 47–54%), Gemma table rows 3–4, and numeric magnitude 4–5 (PC1 40–62%, no clear ordinal progression). The Figure 4 caption conflicts with this, listing Qwen indentation among the cases that collapse to 1-D at middle layers.

status_amendment.public_note: This version's status now reflects the corrections from our accuracy checks: some studies moved between challenge and scope limit, and several no longer count as tests of this version. The level is unchanged, because the challenge at 1-10B still rests on the calendar-circle results the checks confirmed, together with multi-dimensional findings in Gemma 2 and Mistral 7B.
